title: British and Irish Western local-use research review
semantics: These 32 candidates are bounded witnesses, components and bibliography leads, not 32 substantive revisions; source-library acquisition receipts establish hash and delivery extent only.

searches.negative_boundary: Bibliographic lists are historical selections, not exhaustive modern manuscript census.
searches.unexamined_range: Remainder of Weale–Bohatta, especially marginal print identities and all original print colophons.

searches.negative_boundary: No negative claim about unnotated Mass books.

searches.extent: Two saved Sarum search snapshots (25 and 82 hits), exact PDF acquisitions listed in this packet; five-year York and missions queries in final-search log.
searches.negative_boundary: Search results include translations, critical editions, duplicate identities and wrong genre.
searches.unexamined_range: Every unacquired hit and all original title, colophon, Mass order and proper comparison outside explicitly inspected loci; eight retained BIM PDFs are truncated and need fresh whole retrieval.

USU places under Canterbury, but Legg revised its attribution to Sarum; verify with original manuscript.

TCD identifies MS 83 as York missal; dates need detailed catalogue and original.
Core, later additions and erasures are distinct strata. Philip and Mary reconciliation collects are later additions, not a new complete York edition.
Smith preview identifies Canon witness; original catalogue and folios still needed.
Holding in Worcester does not make it Worcester use; original contents uncollated.
Imperfect ff. 1r–142r; Eucharistic chant component, not full missal.

Eeles identifies a 1506 Martin Morin Rouen Sarum print of 277 leaves, with roughly 100 manuscript additions/corrections and a 1498 St Nicholas dedication calendar entry. Print and annotation dates are separate. Aberdeen Breviary is Office, excluded.
Apparently Sarum, produced for Great Easton Essex; traditional Bangor-use attribution discredited; given to Oswestry 1554.
USU 224; 1896 critical edition is later textual witness, not a 1090s print.
Lucas thesis names BL Harley 5289 as Durham Priory missal; direct holding catalogue/folio check remains; preserve as lead, not confirmed Durham recension.

Ninth-century core, tenth-century calendar, eleventh-century quires and later Exeter additions; gift/use date is not core composition. Four of 757 IIIF canvas responses are Image Unavailable placeholders.
Only fragmentary Mass content; no complete local missal inferred.
Abbey identifies MS 37, now bound in two physical volumes. Three HBS editorial volumes are one modern edition, not three medieval manuscripts. Frozen reviewer expected MS 34 in error.
USU 2414; original extent and local use to check against holding library.
IRHT gives possible Canterbury production; later Jumièges gift and USU Winchester indexing do not prove Winchester origin or use.
USU 3369; broad copying interval, substantive comparison open.
Scottish Sarum-related local manuscript; Forbes 1864 edition is distinct evidence object.
Dublin provenance/use requires component inspection; not automatically independent revision.
Carmelite missal ff. 1r–154v; separate c.1300 Irish Sarum antiphonal ff. 156r–171v.
IRHT third-quarter tenth century vs USU 985–1009; origin and dating require reconciliation.
Latin Roman-derived mission book; may be selected Masses, not full missal or distinct source revision.
Weale bibliographic entry only; original title, text and imprint still needed.
Imprint disagreement BnF/Folger; original colophon and delta from 1615/1623 unexamined.

The BIM 1497 PDF (british-acq-sarum-additional-18) is truncated at 864,026,624 of 923,671,404 host-listed bytes; pdfinfo fails. The separate Internet Archive PDF (british-acq-sarum-print-18) matches its 41,087,043-byte host object and has 538 parser-readable pages, but scans Boston Public Library copy Q.402.48 FOLIO, catalogued imperfect with 26 leaves wanting (a1, a6, a7, A1–4, X1, c8, o1–p8, q8). Host-byte completeness does not establish physical-copy or complete-text completeness. The two digitizations are not equated or collated; retain a 1497 print-witness lead without a substantive-revision claim.

Bodleian/Biblissima identify Rawl. C. 892 as a late-twelfth-century Irish Gradual. USU indexes it under Lismore; Buckley discusses Downpatrick Benedictine attribution, while other scholarship argues Lismore. Provenance and intended local use remain disputed. This is a Eucharistic chant component, not a missal or demonstrated Lismore recension.
